Customers can continue using 3.x while they assess 4.0.0, update custom SPL, and validate dashboards, alerts, and data model acceleration.

item.title: PostHog Activity Logs Add-on - v0.6.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**Choosing an index** \- The index field is now empty when you add an input, instead of arriving prefilled. You need the index name to search your events, so it is worth choosing deliberately. The previous default showed up as a new value in the Splunk Cloud picker, which read as though accepting it would create an index.


Short Description:
Collect PostHog activity logs into Splunk as OCSF events. Splunk polls PostHog on a schedule you set, giving you an audit trail of who changed what in your PostHog organization alongside the rest of your security data. Works on Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise.


Description:
PostHog activity logs record who did what in your PostHog organization. Every change to a feature flag, insight, dashboard, or other resource is captured, along with logins and account provisioning changes. This add-on collects that record into Splunk, so you can keep an audit trail alongside the rest of your security data, alert on sensitive changes, and meet compliance requirements. Splunk polls PostHog on a schedule you choose. There is nothing to run or host yourself, and the add-on works the same way on Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise. Events arrive in Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) 1.5.0, so searches and dashboards that already understand OCSF work without a custom parser. Activity maps to three OCSF classes: Entity Management (3004) for changes to resources, Authentication (3002) for logins and logouts, and Account Change (3001) for provisioning. Activity types with no direct OCSF equivalent keep their original PostHog name, so nothing is dropped. Each poll resumes from where the previous one stopped, so entries are collected once. Every event carries the PostHog activity log ID in metadata.uid, which is stable across replays if you need to deduplicate. By default an event records which fields changed, not their values. That answers who changed what and when, which is what an audit trail needs. You can turn on changed values per input when you need the before and after content. Events are timestamped with when the activity happened in PostHog rather than when Splunk indexed them, so historical searches reflect real history. The add-on requires a PostHog personal API key with the activity_log:read scope. Activity logs are available on the PostHog Boost, Scale and Enterprise packages.

Release Notes:
``` EventTimeline 1.0.3 is the initial public Splunkbase release. Highlights: • Converts Splunk saved-search alerts into normalized investigation findings. • Generates chronological AWS CloudTrail timelines organized into before-alert, alert-trigger, and after-alert phases. • Uses manual timeline generation by default to reduce search-head workload. • Provides optional automatic timeline generation through Setup. • Supports configurable investigation windows from 30 minutes to 24 hours. • Includes MITRE ATT&CK and kill-chain views. • Provides identity, assumed-role, resource, account, source-IP, access-key, event-name, and event-ID pivots. • Includes a manual timeline generator for analyst-led investigations. • Provides raw-event inspection and Markdown or CSV export. • Includes timeline search status, diagnostics, truncation reporting, retry handling, deduplication, and health monitoring. • Includes an in-app Saved Search Guide with field requirements and CloudTrail examples. • Adds bounded searches and hydration limits for large CloudTrail environments. • Does not require an AI provider or external analysis service. • Does not include prebuilt detection content; it operates with existing Splunk saved searches and alerts. ```


Short Description:
Convert AWS CloudTrail saved-search alerts into chronological investigation timelines with normalized context, MITRE mapping, entity pivots, manual searches, and exportable evidence.


Description:
EventTimeline turns AWS CloudTrail alerts from Splunk saved searches into structured, chronological investigations. When a saved search triggers, EventTimeline creates a normalized finding containing the alert context, actor, resource, source IP, account, API action, severity, and event timestamp. Analysts can then fetch related CloudTrail activity for a selected investigation window and review what happened before, during, and after the alert. EventTimeline includes chronological evidence views, MITRE ATT&CK and kill-chain context, identity and resource pivots, raw-event access, timeline filtering, Markdown export, a manual timeline generator, and timeline health diagnostics. The app does not include proprietary detection content or require an AI provider. It works with your existing CloudTrail saved searches and allows teams to retain control over their detection logic and investigation workflow.

item.title: TheHive/Cortex - v4.2.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\# Release Notes - v4.2.2: "The Pollen Sieve" 🌼 \## Summary Version 4.2.2 is a \*\*bug-fix release\*\* about things that used to fall through without a sound. A custom field of type \`url\` was dropped from every alert and case with no error at all; an empty "Job SID" let the create action fail deep inside the add-on instead of stopping at the form. Both are fixed, and the add-on now \*\*says something\*\* when it drops a custom field instead of staying silent. Splunk Cloud administrators (\`sc\_admin\`) also regain write access to the views and navigation. No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is a safe, drop-in update from v4.2.1. \## Improvements & Bug Fixes \### 🧩 Alert Actions: \`url\` custom fields are no longer dropped (\[#133]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/133)) \- \*\*Root cause\*\*: custom field values are only forwarded when their type is recognised by a chain handling \`string\`, \`boolean\`, \`integer\`, \`float\` and \`date\`. The \`url\` type, available since TheHive 5.1, was missing from that chain, so the field was skipped. The alert or case was still created, minus the field, and \*\*nothing was logged\*\* — the value simply never arrived. \- \*\*Fix\*\*: \`url\` carries a plain string value and is now handled exactly like \`string\`. Both "Create a new alert" and "Create a new case" are affected, as they share the same parsing routine. \- \*\*No more silence\*\*: a custom field dropped because its type is unmapped, or because its value does not match its declared type, is now logged as a warning (\`THC-117\`) naming both the field and the type. A future unknown type will be visible in the logs instead of costing a day of troubleshooting. \- \*\*Regression tests\*\*: the parsing routine gains its first unit tests. Every TheHive custom field type is now asserted to survive, and the "dropped but logged" behaviour is asserted too. \### 🖥️ Dashboards: the Job SID is now required (\[#132]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/132)) \- \*\*Root cause\*\*: "Job SID (input data)" was optional in the \*Create a new case\* and \*Create a new alert\* panels. Leaving it empty produced an empty \`| loadjob\`, and the failure surfaced far from its cause — a \`FileNotFoundError\` followed by \`UnboundLocalError: local variable 'rf' referenced before assignment\`, deep inside the alert action base. \- \*\*Fix\*\*: Splunk Simple XML has no \`required\` attribute, so the field now drives a token and the action panel depends on it. The action cannot run until a SID is entered, and the label carries a \`\*\` like the other mandatory fields. \### ☁️ Splunk Cloud: \`sc\_admin\` can write views and navigation \- \`metadata/default.meta\` granted write access on \`\[views]\` and \`\[nav]\` to the \`admin\` role only. Splunk Cloud customers hold \*\*\`sc\_admin\`\*\*, not \`admin\`, so those knowledge objects were unreachable for them. Release Notes:
**Bug fix release** — reported by an external reviewer. **Recommended upgrade for anyone running v1.0.6 or earlier**, especially environments with dual-stack hosts or multi-homed machines. ### The bug The WithSecure Elements API returns `details.hostIpAddress` as a single JSON string that concatenates every IP the host is bound to, separated by spaces: ``` "hostIpAddress": "192.168.110.128/24 192.168.171.128/24 10.0.0.5/8" ``` Splunk's `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS = json` stored this as one flat string, so a search like: ``` index=main sourcetype="withsecure:epp:security_event" "details.hostIpAddress"="192.168.171.128/24" ``` never matched events where that address was not the first one in the string. In the reporter's test corpus 13/53 events had two IPs and were affected — the same pattern is present on any host with multiple network interfaces or a dual-stack (IPv4 + link-local) configuration. ### The fix A single search-time `EVAL` calculated field on the `security_event` sourcetype that splits the string into a real multivalue field: ``` [withsecure:epp:security_event] EVAL-details.hostIpAddress = split('details.hostIpAddress', " ") ``` **Search-time only:** * no impact on ingestion, no re-indexing needed * applies retroactively to events already in the index * 100 % reversible (remove the line to go back to a flat string) After upgrading, the following now behave consistently on every IP the host reports: * exact-match: `details.hostIpAddress="192.168.171.128/24"` * `IN()`: `details.hostIpAddress IN ("10.0.0.5/8", "192.168.171.128/24")` * `| mvexpand details.hostIpAddress` — one row per IP * `mvcount(details.hostIpAddress)` — actual count of IPs * CIM `src_ip` alias — respects the multivalue ### Upgrade safety Non-destructive in-place upgrade. KV Store checkpoints, input configuration, and existing indexed events are preserved.


Short Description:

It ingests EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections through OAuth2-authenticated modular inputs, enabling centralized security event analysis in Splunk. The add-on maps collected events to CIM endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process tags, facilitating correlation with other security data sources. Two modular inputs handle data collection: withsecure_epp_input retrieves endpoint protection events, while withsecure_bcd_input collects EDR broad context detection incidents. The application functionality remains centered on securely sending selected Splunk search results to MISP through the mispfusepush command or the MISPFuse alert action. ## **Compatibility** * Splunk Enterprise 8.0.0 or later * Supported Splunk Python runtimes: 3.7, 3.9, and 3.13 * MISP 2.5.x * UCC 6.5.3 used for application generation Splunk Cloud deployment remains subject to AppInspect and Cloud vetting for the exact submitted package. ## **Fixed** * Fixed SLIM validation failures caused by the previous Splunk Enterprise version constraints not intersecting with the Enterprise versions recognized by the Packaging Toolkit catalog. * Changed the manifest requirement from >\=9.0.0 to the verified >\=8.0.0 boundary. * Preserved backward-compatible Python runtime selection without removing Python 3.13 support on newer Splunk releases. ## **Functionality** MISPFuse provides: * Multiple configurable MISP server connections. * Encrypted MISP API-key storage through Splunk credential management. * Save-time MISP connection validation. * Manual IOC and event submission using the mispfusepush SPL command. * Scheduled event submission through a custom alert action. * Four bundled mapping templates: * network\_ioc * file\_hashes * email\_phishing * passthrough * single\_event, per\_row, and by\_field event grouping. * Splunk multivalue-field handling. * MISP describeTypes validation against the connected MISP server. * Configurable distribution, threat level, analysis state, tags, to\_ids, and event publishing. * Proxy support and TLS certificate verification. * API-key and proxy-credential redaction from connection errors. * Response-size limits, disabled redirects, and connection/read timeouts. * No platform-specific native runtime libraries in the release package. ## **Validation** Release 2.2.4 was validated with: * Splunk Packaging Toolkit 1.2.8 using standalone slim validate. * 41 unit tests across Python 3.7, Python 3.9, and Python 3.13. * UCC 6.5.3 build and post-build package verification. * Splunk AppInspect 4.3.0 precert validation with Cloud tags. * Release checks for compiled Python files and native binaries. * Exact and hash-locked runtime dependencies. ## Release Notes:
# Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk 3.4.0 ## Important compatibility notice - Version 3.4.0 requires Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform 10.2 or later with Python 3.13. Do not configure or enable this version on an earlier Splunk platform release. - Splunk Enterprise 9.4 does not provide the Python 3.13 runtime selected by this add-on and is not supported by version 3.4.0. - On an unsupported Splunk platform release, the Inputs or Configuration page can fail to load and display the following Python handler error: `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'type'`. This error indicates an incompatible Python runtime, not a Meraki credential or input configuration failure. - All modular inputs and Python REST handlers declare `python.required = 3.13`. - The Home dashboard displays a compatibility warning when the current search head runs an unsupported Splunk platform release. - Customers who must temporarily remain on an older Splunk platform release can download version 3.3.0 from the Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk page on Splunkbase. Version 3.3.0 does not contain fixes and features added in later releases. ## What's new - Standardizes all current Dashboard Studio charts on the shared Cisco C3 visualization palette. Informational, healthy, caution, critical, comparison, and unknown states now retain the same color meaning across workspaces. - Uses outlined markers and connects null values on every Dashboard Studio line chart so isolated samples and intermittent collection gaps remain readable. - Pins assurance-alert pie slices to label-based C3 severity colors so critical, warning, informational, and unknown categories cannot change meaning when a category is absent or the result order changes. - Adds a TA API health tab to Data Collection Health that measures only Meraki Dashboard API calls attributed to this add-on. The panels use `meraki:apirequestshistory` events whose User-Agent contains `SplunkAddOnForCiscoMeraki`. - Adds request volume, success rate, rate-limit indicators, operation frequency, response outcomes, OAuth client identity, failure details, and bounded estimates of the Splunk platform license volume used by API request-history events generated by the add-on. - Normalizes matching API request-history `userAgent` values to `SplunkAddOnForCiscoMeraki` before indexing. User-Agent values for other API clients remain unchanged, and the dashboard recognizes historical events that contain the longer SDK-generated value. - Keeps the API Data dashboard as the organization-wide API exploration workspace and links to it from Data Collection Health. - Adds an hourly Meraki ingest chart and a sourcetype table that combines event counts, indexed volume, data freshness, expected collection interval, and health status. ## Fixed issues - Applies the complete Magic Eight index-time parsing contract to all 43 packaged `meraki:*` sourcetypes. The add-on now defines explicit JSON event boundaries and timestamp scan limits, disables punctuation annotation and automatic sourcetype learning, and preserves ingest time for snapshot data that has no single event timestamp. - Replaces `dedup` commands before grouped dashboard aggregations with `stats`-based reduction. History panels retain every transition, while snapshot and repeatable API records are reduced by their logical identity before distributions are calculated. - Removes redundant `spath` parsing and event-level `mvexpand` work from structured Meraki JSON dashboard searches. Selective filters now run in base searches, while response summaries aggregate extracted fields before bounded presentation transforms. - Fixes Dashboard Studio rendering errors on the TA API health tab by using a transforming base search with a single post-process level. - Fixes API health empty states so summary panels display numeric zeroes when no add-on-attributed request-history events are available, while detailed charts and tables remain empty. - Fixes Dashboard Studio grid validation errors on the TA API health tab by aligning the organization input with the panel grid below it. - Fixes the rate-limit summary so it uses the correct aggregated field. - Prevents API requests made by unrelated clients from affecting the add-on's API health measurements. - Removes redundant broad `sourcetype="meraki:*"` constraints from dashboard searches that already use the `meraki_index` macro. Exact sourcetype filters, including `meraki:apirequestshistory` for TA API health, remain in place. - Adds Home dashboard guidance and a direct macro-editor link so administrators can scope `meraki_index` to production indexes without dropping its Meraki sourcetype constraint. ## Upgrade notes - Existing input configuration and checkpoints remain compatible. - Customers running version 3.3.10 should upgrade to version 3.4.0. This release includes the bounded pagination and streaming changes introduced in version 3.3.11 to prevent scripted-input out-of-memory failures. - Uses `package/VERSION` as the only release-version source. The build stamps `app.conf`, `app.manifest`, the UCC UI configuration, and the numeric Splunk build identifier in generated artifacts without modifying tracked metadata. Repeated builds of the same version advance the prior successful artifact's build number, such as 3400, 3401, and 3402 for version 3.4.0. - Adds a release-check command that builds the package, runs unit and lint gates, blocks AppInspect errors and failures, and can create a disposable Splunk Docker lab for modular-input smoke testing under Python 3.13. ## Validation - The Python 3.13 release gate reports 96 passing tests. Lint, syntax, package metadata, and archive-safety checks also pass. - Build-only runs produce `Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki-3.4.0.tgz` with version 3.4.0 and a successively increasing build number without installing the add-on. - Splunk AppInspect 4.3.0 reports 134 successful checks, nine warnings, and no errors or failures with Splunk Cloud precertification scope. - The release workflow performs build and verification without restarting Splunk software.


Description:
The Splunk Add-on for Cisco Meraki provides comprehensive network observability and security monitoring across your Meraki organizations. This add-on collects rich data via Cisco Meraki REST APIs and webhooks to deliver insights into network performance, security, and device health. Sample visualizations are also provided to help explore the data and create custom dashboards. The add-on provides Common Information Model (CIM) compatible knowledge to integrate with other Splunk solutions, including Splunk Enterprise Security and Splunk App for PCI Compliance. Data collection can be customized through scheduled API polling and real-time webhooks to match your monitoring requirements. Security & Event Monitoring: • Organization-wide security event tracking • Air Marshal wireless threat detection • Network device logging and audit trails • Rapid network alerts via webhooks Infrastructure & Performance Insights: • Device availability and uptime monitoring • Wireless and switching performance metrics • Ethernet status and packet loss analytics • Environmental sensor data tracking • Top device rankings by usage and utilization • Energy consumption monitoring for switches Network Operations: • Configuration change tracking • SD-WAN and VPN performance monitoring • Cellular gateway uplink status • API usage analytics and optimization • License and firmware auditing Supported Cisco Meraki Devices: • Access Points • Security Appliances • Switches • Cameras • Environmental Sensors • Cellular Gateways

item.title: Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk - v3.2.44 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**Important for upgrades:** Before migrating saved searches or alerts, review the legacy dynamic-sourcetype upgrade checks in the User Guide included with the TA. ##### What's New modal * **Release notes surface automatically:** Each release now opens a polished What's New modal inside the add-on, with a compact section navigator and a direct link to the full User Guide. * **Explicit per-user suppression:** Closing the modal normally hides it only for the current page visit, so the release notes return the next time the add-on opens. Selecting **Do not show again** before closing stores the suppressed version for the signed-in Splunk user; a newer release appears automatically, and the modal can still be reopened from Application Setup. * **Restart-free, cluster-consistent preference updates:** The user-scoped `ta_cisco_catalyst_ui.conf` now has an explicit reload trigger and Search Head Cluster replication declaration, so saving **Do not show again** no longer requests a restart and remains consistent across cluster members. * **Single release-note source:** The modal renders the bounded **Current release at a glance** subsection from this User Guide Markdown, so its concise announcement and the full guide cannot drift into separately maintained release-note files. ##### Application Setup release badges * **Current release callouts:** Input Type menus now show compact **New!** and **Enhanced!** badges beside this release's highlighted inputs across Catalyst Center, Cyber Vision, SD-WAN, and ISE. A selected highlighted input keeps its badge in the closed control. * **New NetFlow workspace:** The SD-WAN **NetFlow** tab now carries the same compact **New!** badge so operators can spot the new listener, dependency, and destination-index workflow immediately. * **Release-only metadata:** Badges come from one release-maintained index and are display-only. They do not rename input types, change saved values, issue API requests, or alter collection behavior, and can be updated or removed independently before a future release. ##### Guided SD-WAN NetFlow workspace * **Requirements first:** Step 1 checks all four required Stream and Cisco packages before the operator changes a listener or SD-WAN Manager configuration. The live result is limited to the current Splunk Web node and tells the operator where remote collector and indexer placement must be verified. * **Five numbered steps:** The workflow continues through protocol choice, listener configuration, destination-index confirmation, and one-edge canary validation with explicit Back and Next actions. * **Visible prerequisite guard:** A live preflight now warns when App for Stream (1809) or Stream Wire Data (5234) is missing, disabled, or unverifiable. Destination-index requests and the Stream configuration link remain paused until App for Stream is ready, preventing an absent custom endpoint from appearing as a generic 500 error. The warning distinguishes the current-node check from Wire Data placement that must also be verified on every indexer. * **Progressive disclosure:** Only the active task is shown, and optional listener tuning, exporter allowlists, capacity guidance, and configuration-file details remain collapsed until needed. * **Saved forwarder identity explained:** A populated **Stream Forwarder ID** is loaded from the existing `stream_forwarder_id` value in `Splunk_TA_stream/local/inputs.conf`; the page neither generates nor hard-codes it, and a blank value continues to let Stream use the host name. * **Current product terminology:** Customer-facing UI and guide text now use **Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager**; **vManage** remains only in explicit legacy labels, literal compatibility signals, fields, URLs, and old release names. ##### UI build dependency security * **Dependabot remediation:** The React build and development toolchain now resolves the patched Babel, Webpack development server, WebSocket, proxy, YAML, CSS, URI, glob, and related transitive packages required by the repository's security advisories. * **Unused parser removed:** The unused `image-size` development dependency was removed, eliminating its unpatched image-parser paths without changing the shipped UI or runtime React/UCC libraries. * **Deterministic security floor:** Targeted npm overrides keep transitive packages above their fixed versions while preserving the existing Splunk React/UCC runtime contract and reproducible `npm ci` builds. ##### Catalyst Center scheduled-report namespace * **Report sourcetypes aligned with Catalyst Center:** Newly collected scheduled reports now use `cisco:dnac:inventory:report`, `cisco:dnac:compliance:report`, and `cisco:dnac:report` instead of the older `cisco:catalyst:center:*` report namespace. * **Dual-read transition eventtypes:** `cisco_dnac_inventory_report`, `cisco_dnac_compliance_report`, and `cisco_dnac_report` each search the exact current and previous sourcetypes. `cisco_catalyst_center_reports` searches all three report families. Historical events are neither renamed nor reindexed. * **Visible migration contract:** Application Setup displays an amber migration warning plus **Current sourcetype**, **Previous sourcetype**, and **Transition eventtype** columns. Data Collection Health uses the umbrella eventtype so current and retained report data remain visible together. * **Readable migration table:** The report description now lives inside each row's expandable **More info** panel, leaving the three migration identifiers enough room to remain readable in the default split-panel layout. * **Report identity remains stable:** `report_name`, `report_type`, `report_category`, `cisco_catalyst_host`, and `collection_timestamp` continue to identify the report definition, family, controller, and snapshot time. Arbitrary report rows are not assigned a payload-specific CIM tag without a validated schema. ##### Resizable Application Setup workspace * **Drag-resizable product and configuration panels:** Add Input pages now default to a 70/30 product-information/configuration layout and provide a center splitter that can be dragged directly with a mouse or pointer between bounded 30/70 and 70/30 layouts. Left/Right and Home/End keys provide an accessible alternative, double-click restores the 70/30 default, the current ratio remains visible, and narrow viewports continue to stack the panels automatically. ##### Stable Generic Custom API sourcetypes * **One sourcetype per product family:** Generic Custom API events now use `cisco:dnac:custom`, `cisco:sdwan:custom`, `cisco:ise:custom`, or `cisco:cybervision:custom` instead of creating a sourcetype for every selected REST endpoint. * **Endpoint identity remains searchable:** Every custom event includes a normalized, bounded `endpoint_name` plus the cataloged `endpoint_path`, so searches and dashboards can select an endpoint without expanding sourcetype cardinality. * **Identity fields explained in context:** The expandable **More info** panel for every product's Generic Custom API sourcetype now explains how `endpoint_name` groups a selected operation, how `endpoint_path` preserves its configured catalog route, and when SD-WAN adds `target_device_id` for device-scoped collection. * **CIM-safe shared metadata:** The stable families retain the add-on's universal `vendor`, `product`, `vendor_product`, and `app` fields. Payload-specific CIM mappings remain with dedicated inputs because arbitrary endpoint JSON does not share one truthful data-model contract. ##### Stable ISE policy and analytics sourcetypes * **One policy family:** Newly collected RADIUS and TACACS+ policy sets and authorization rules use `cisco:ise:policy`. The bounded `policy_protocol` field identifies `radius` or `tacacs`; `policy_record_type` identifies `policy_set` or `authorization_rule`; `endpoint_name` and `endpoint_path` preserve the originating Open API surface. * **One analytics family:** General, registry, hardware, applications, and full endpoint report rows now use `cisco:ise:analytics`. `report_type` identifies the bounded report family and `report_name` preserves the source filename. * **Dual-read transition eventtypes:** `cisco_ise_policy` and `cisco_ise_analytics_reports` search their current family plus retained history. The protocol/record and report-specific eventtypes shown in Application Setup provide exact old-and-new searches. Historical events are not renamed or reindexed. * **Visible migration contract:** The ISE product card displays an amber migration warning plus **Current sourcetype**, **Previous sourcetype**, and **Transition eventtype** columns. Descriptions and identity-field guidance remain available through each row's **More info** panel. * **CIM-safe scope:** Both current families expose universal `vendor`, `product`, `vendor_product`, and `app` fields. Policy snapshots are configuration state, not authentication transactions, and variable analytics report rows are not assigned a payload-specific CIM tag without representative schema validation. ##### Data Collection Health sourcetype migration roll-up * **Current-family health:** Data Collection Health rolls retained Catalyst Center, endpoint-derived Custom API, SD-WAN firewall/access/syslog, and ISE policy/analytics sourcetypes into their current canonical families before calculating freshness, status, volume, and chart series. Historical events remain unchanged in the indexes. * **No false retired-feed outages:** Retained names no longer age into separate Critical rows after their current replacement is healthy. The retired ISE Security Group event feed is excluded because the current Security Group Tags workflow refreshes KV Store data rather than indexing a replacement event sourcetype. * **Physical evidence remains available:** Data Quality, scheduled-report evidence, and onboarding **Processed Sourcetypes** retain physical names for migration and routing diagnosis. The Cyber Vision catch-all `cisco:cybervision:custom` family is now included in Data Quality and uses the same 60-minute health expectation as the other Custom API families. * **NetFlow ingest health:** A fifth Overview status card and a dedicated NetFlow tab now track the Stream-owned `stream:netflow` path. The tab shows freshness and selected-window license volume, a 30-minute arrival trend, processing-host throughput and pipeline evidence, destination-index activity, and the top indexed host values without scanning raw high-volume flow events. * **Accurate SD-WAN text-syslog output list:** Application Setup now lists only the five current text-routing destinations. It excludes the separate REST Audit Logs sourcetype and retained per-message history, while explaining that firewall output is conditional and modern Unified Logging delivers covered security events as `stream:netflow`. Transition eventtypes continue to search historical names. ##### SD-WAN NetFlow guidance * **Reproducible SD-WAN telemetry runbook:** Application Setup and the User Guide now distinguish the exact live-tested v9, v10, and syslog paths from conditional signal families, explain that the listener form manages receiver 0 only, and add a stop-on-drift Manager preview and canary gate. * **Production sourcetype contract:** Splunk Stream continues to index production NetFlow and IPFIX events as `stream:netflow`; this TA does not change that metadata and supplies bounded search-time CIM knowledge for the Stream-owned events. * **Four-step NetFlow setup:** The SD-WAN **NetFlow** tab now behaves as a compact setup flow instead of one long page: choose NetFlow v9/HSL or IPFIX v10/Unified Logging, configure the listener, confirm the destination index, and validate packages and packets. Back/Next controls keep only the current task visible, while optional listener restrictions remain behind a clearly labeled control. * **Corrected Unified Logging cutover:** The guidance no longer assumes that UTD text syslog remains available in parallel after Unified Logging is enabled. It directs operators to capture a bounded UTD syslog baseline before cutover and validate the corresponding IPFIX records afterward. * **Local Stream listener setup:** The tab can now read and save the local UDP NetFlow listener managed by Splunk Stream through native authenticated Splunk configuration endpoints. It detects up to 64 IPv4/IPv6 addresses assigned to the host so an operator can select one or enter a different valid bind address. It writes the owning app's `Splunk_TA_stream/local/inputs.conf` and `streamfwd.conf`, validates the app URL, bind IP, UDP port, sender filters, and a bounded 1–32 decoder-thread setting, and never changes `streamfwdlog.conf` or restarts Splunk. The form explains exactly what the save action changes and clearly marks the documented user-run restart required after saving. * **Inline destination-index editing:** Each Stream-owned NetFlow definition can now change its destination index directly in the Cisco add-on. **Edit index** stays beside the value it controls and opens a responsive full-width editor so the index, sourcetype, status, and actions remain aligned at narrower widths. The editor defaults unset definitions to `default`, reuses the same visible non-internal index choices as the other input forms, changes only the definition's `index`, and verifies the saved value without altering its fields, filters, mode, ownership, or Stream-managed sourcetype. Definitions owned by another app remain read-only here and link to Splunk App for Stream. * **Single production Stream definition:** The destination-index panel now promotes `cisco_hsl_cisco_hsl_netflow` as the authoritative Cisco HSL/IPFIX definition when it is installed and enabled. Disabled, generic, or comparison definitions remain available under **Other Stream definitions** for troubleshooting instead of appearing as equal production choices. If multiple definitions are enabled, the page warns that overlapping filters can duplicate indexed flow records and directs operators to keep exactly one intended production definition enabled. * **Stream HEC setup:** The same tab checks HTTP Event Collector readiness and, when authorized, creates or enables the managed `streamfwd` HEC input in one click. Splunk retains the generated token; the Cisco add-on does not display it, log it, or store it in browser state. * **Live deployment dependency checks:** The tab identifies the Stream Forwarder, App for Stream, Wire Data, and conditional Cisco Catalyst Enhanced NetFlow packages, shows live installed and latest-version status, and offers filtered **Install** or **Update** links alongside each Splunkbase listing. Missing, disabled, or unverifiable App for Stream status now pauses destination-index access instead of surfacing a generic endpoint error; missing Wire Data is called out for both search-head and indexer placement. It configures only the local listener and HEC readiness; SD-WAN Manager export and the applicable Stream definition remain separate deployment steps. * **Configured Inputs lifecycle:** A saved receiver now appears as **NetFlow Listener** in the SDWAN group on Application Setup. Operators can enable or disable it, jump directly back to the NetFlow editor, or delete both managed Stream stanzas from the same actions menu. Every listener mutation retains the explicit user-run restart boundary. * **Stream-owned NetFlow sourcetype:** The SD-WAN product card and NetFlow tab identify `stream:netflow` as the unchanged production sourcetype and direct operators to the stable `cisco_netflow` eventtype for CIM-scoped searches. * **Stable CIM eventtype:** `eventtype=cisco_netflow` searches `sourcetype=stream:netflow NOT event_name=netFlowOptions` and carries the `network` and `communicate` tags. Saved searches, alerts, dashboards, and data-model validation should use this contract. * **CIM 8.6 Network Traffic normalization:** Bounded search-time mappings cover production `stream:netflow` for NetFlow v9 and IPFIX v10. They normalize exporter identity, endpoints, interfaces, ports, IP/transport versions, direction, duration, actions, policy/rule identity, users, TCP flags, VLANs, and existing Stream byte/packet/application fields. Options metadata remains excluded from the Network Traffic eventtype. * **Reliable Stream configuration namespace:** Listener reads, creates, updates, toggles, and deletes now use the explicit `nobody/Splunk_TA_stream` REST namespace, so a missing stanza cannot be created accidentally under the signed-in user's current app namespace. * **Dedicated-index and clock-skew verification:** NetFlow validation now follows the configured `netflow` destination index, verifies Cisco decoding through enterprise fields rather than contradictory base searches, and includes an index-time canary for exporters whose clocks are wrong. * **Measurement-led capacity planning:** Removed the unsupported fixed per-device volume estimate and fixed ingest multiplier. The guide now derives daily volume and p95 collector load from a representative pilot and requires UDP-loss, template, CPU, queue, and indexing-lag evidence before production qualification. * **Manual fallback boundary:** Direct `streamfwd.conf` editing and App for Stream mode repair are now labeled advanced fallback procedures. Application Setup remains the primary listener and destination-index workflow. ##### User guide navigation and search * **Readable Heavy Forwarder tuning table:** The tuning reference now fits the guide viewport without horizontal scrolling, keeps the 30-second load-balancing default as the starting value, and separates the single-pipeline baseline from a measured two-pipeline override that requires CPU, memory, network, and queue headroom. * **Descriptive browser tabs:** Application Setup, Add Input, Data Collection Health, and User Guide tabs now include the Cisco Catalyst Add-on name so they remain identifiable beside other Splunk pages. The guide sets its final browser title explicitly so Splunk does not append a platform-version suffix. * **Reliable search navigation:** Pressing Enter or **Next** immediately after changing a guide query applies the current query and navigates to the first visible document result, excluding the print-only contents list. **Clear** removes the query and returns the reader to the top of the guide. * **Compact navigation rails:** **Jump to a task** is collapsed by default, and the **On this page** rail no longer repeats the operator-directory links as duplicate headings. * **Executable sizing search:** The Device Health event-size example now opens with `index=main` instead of a literal index placeholder; administrators replace `main` with their Cisco data index. * **Executable SD-WAN upgrade check:** The legacy-sourcetype audit now opens with `index=main`; administrators are told to replace `main` with the index that holds their SD-WAN syslog. * **Copy-only migration example:** The SD-WAN before/after sourcetype example remains syntax-highlighted and copyable without presenting a misleading **Open in Search** action for its mutually exclusive alternatives. * **Customer-controlled time ranges:** Routine User Guide SPL examples rely on the Splunk time picker. The NetFlow clock-skew recovery canary is the documented exception: operators select **All time**, then use a bounded recent index-time window so bad exporter timestamps cannot hide fresh ingestion. * **Consistent index scope:** Customer-facing SPL examples use executable index names instead of wildcard or literal placeholder values. Most examples use `main`; the NetFlow workflow uses its dedicated `netflow` destination index. Operators replace either example with the index configured for their data. * **Persistent upgrade-check link:** Every Cisco Catalyst Add-on release panel now links directly to the legacy dynamic-sourcetype upgrade checks so the required pre-migration validation remains visible in current and future TA release notes. The separate NetFlow and Enterprise Networking app histories remain unchanged. ##### SD-WAN RFC 5424 syslog routing * **Prominent legacy-sourcetype warnings:** The SD-WAN syslog routing reference now includes amber migration notices for the operational, firewall, and access-control consolidation boundaries. Historical data keeps its indexed sourcetype. * **Explicit firewall transition eventtypes:** The routing table shows each raw `%FW-*` signal, current sourcetype, previous sourcetype, and dual-read eventtype. Use `eventtype=cisco_sdwan_firewall` for the whole family or the per-message eventtype shown in the table while old data remains searchable. * **CIM-safe firewall families:** `eventtype=cisco_sdwan_firewall_traffic` carries `network` and `communicate` tags for session, pass, drop, and summary records. `eventtype=cisco_sdwan_firewall_alerts` carries the `alert` tag for threshold and host-protection messages. Unknown future `%FW-*` mnemonics still land in the stable firewall sourcetype with identity fields, but are not forced into an unsupported CIM data model. * **RFC 5424 operational messages restored:** Generic IOS-XE `%FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:` messages now route to `cisco:sdwan:syslog` regardless of whether the transport envelope uses the legacy numeric header, a month-name IOS header, RFC 5424, the literal `BOM` marker, or a Unicode BOM. * **Signal identity explained in context:** The `cisco:sdwan:syslog` **More info** panel now explains the canonical `event_id` and its `facility`, optional `subfacility`, `severity_id`, readable `severity`, and `mnemonic` components so operators can choose exact-signal or family-level field filters. * **ISO event time preserved:** RFC 5424 `1 `envelopes now position timestamp parsing on the ISO timestamp instead of silently falling back to index time. * **Remaining fixed-route consolidation completed:** Smart Licensing and DMI errors now use `cisco:sdwan:syslog`. ACL and SGACL now share `cisco:sdwan:access:logs`, where their specialized parsers remain isolated from unrelated operational syslog. `eventtype=cisco_sdwan_access` carries CIM Network Traffic tags, while per-signal dual-read eventtypes preserve exact searches across new and historical data. * **Purpose-built routes preserved:** Both legacy `[**]`-delimited UTD payloads and native IOS-XE `%UTD--:` records use `cisco:sdwan:utd:logs`; SD-WAN Manager audit keeps its distinct sourcetype because its wire format and collection semantics remain different. Historical events are not rewritten. * **Bounded matching:** The generic rule requires a Cisco `%FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:` identifier and does not treat unrelated percentage text such as `95%:` as IOS-XE syslog. ##### Catalyst Center Client query windows * **Complete Client query windows:** Client collection now supplies the explicit `startTime` and `endTime` required by affected Catalyst Center 2.3.7.x deployments. It reuses one stable window across every page, covers the configured polling interval plus a bounded overlap of up to five minutes, and initially queries the previous completed minute. When Catalyst Center returns error code `14006` on the first page, the collector validates the controller-suggested ready `endTime` and retries once with the same-duration window shifted backward by no more than five minutes. Generic, repeated, unsafe, and later-page failures abort the poll without publishing a partial snapshot. ##### Catalyst Center ITSI large-fleet sizing guidance * **Scalable, fail-closed Device Health pagination:** The Device Health and network-device inventory REST walks now use one bounded paginator and request up to 500 records per page. A controller falls back to the legacy 20-record size only when the first request explicitly rejects the `limit`; timeouts, throttling, server errors, malformed data, generic request failures, and later-page failures abort the poll. Inventory count-before/count-after checks, duplicate UUID detection, and a 256 MiB response cap reject unstable or oversized walks. Events and heartbeats carry one collection ID plus expected/actual output counts for reconciliation. * **Scalable Assurance Issue collection:** Issue collection now prefers the count-aware `/dna/data/api/v1/assuranceIssues` API with a fixed 24-hour query window, 25-record pagination, five-request-per-second proactive pacing, duplicate/count/byte checks, and direct issue/site/device metadata mapping. Missing device identity uses deduplicated point lookups for up to 10 devices or one count-verified bulk inventory walk above that threshold. Only an explicit first-request endpoint-unavailable response selects the bounded legacy collector; other and later-page failures abort the poll. The legacy path shares caches and pacing across statuses, removes the fixed 15-second per-issue delay, and reports `status=recovering` because its unpaged list cannot prove completeness. * **Shared controller protection:** Every Catalyst Center API input now has an 80%-of-interval poll deadline, request timeouts clipped to the remaining budget, a 30-second maximum `Retry-After` with jitter, deterministic process-start staggering, and a controller-scoped request governor shared by modular-input processes on the same Heavy Forwarder. Device Health reserves its documented 20-requests/minute slots; Site and current Security Advisory calls reserve their documented 100-requests/minute slots. The controller identity is hashed in the local coordination filename; credentials and payloads are never stored there. * **Security Advisory and Compliance N+1 removal:** Both collectors take one bounded, count-verified device inventory snapshot and join device/site metadata in memory. Security Advisory uses the current 500-record paginated advisory and affected-device APIs, derives severity totals from the completed current snapshot instead of calling the sunset aggregate API, reconciles every relationship walk with `deviceCount`, caps advisory/device relationships and response bytes, and fails the whole cycle on an incomplete relationship. Older controllers use the bounded sunset API family and report `status=recovering`. Compliance now bounds both status/detail walks and no longer performs two enrichment calls per device. * **Bounded secondary snapshots:** Site Topology, Client, and Audit Logs now share repeated-page, page-count, record-count, response-byte, and fail-closed guards. Site Topology events include snapshot ID, sequence, and expected count; all three inputs report pagination and output completeness. Application Traffic, SWIM, and Network Health also reject malformed, oversized, or over-limit single responses and enforce the shared output deadline. * **Compact change checkpoints:** Issue, Security Advisory, and Client Health store SHA-256 content fingerprints in 16 batched KV Store ledger documents instead of reading and writing one full checkpoint document per record. A bounded compatibility migration preserves the first 1,000 legacy states; any excess is emitted at most once and then uses the ledger. Stale hashes are removed on a rotating 45-day schedule, and the ledger advances only after event output succeeds. * **Capacity-aware Device Health setup:** The production default and large-fleet baseline are now 900 seconds. A controller inventory above 1,000 devices at a shorter interval emits `capacity_warning=true`; Data Collection Health uses the same 15-minute freshness expectation, and the 900-second setting remains a coverage ceiling because the source query covers only the previous 15 minutes. * **Splunk Cloud-safe collection health:** The active React Data Collection Health dashboard now derives scheduled-report, process, and resource status exclusively from indexed events, structured poll heartbeats, and accelerated data. It no longer runs SPL `rest` searches for local server or input configuration, which also avoids incorrectly treating search-head configuration as the Heavy Forwarder collector configuration. Automated tests keep its expected intervals aligned with `default/inputs.conf`. * **Accurate duplicate and error diagnostics:** Dataset-specific SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring source paths now collapse to their parent input stanza before duplicate detection, so one consolidated input is not mistaken for many inputs. SD-WAN Health device discovery treats a short final page as normal completion and fails closed on malformed, repeated, or oversized walks. TA internal-log parsing retains bounded 100 KB/1,000-line tracebacks, and oversized vendor bodies preserve both their opening context and final root-cause text. * **Workload-aware sizing chapter:** The operator guide now separates Catalyst Center API polling, syslog, NetFlow/IPFIX/HSL, and Splunk ingest/search capacity instead of routing the general sizing link to a NetFlow-only subsection. * **ITSI input planning example:** A worked five-cluster, 26,000–29,000-device example sizes Device Health, Issue, Security Advisory, and Site Topology separately, documents uneven regional distribution, and uses a measured regional-HF starting layout. * **Evidence boundary made explicit:** Heavy Forwarder tuning improves forwarding and queue reliability but does not accelerate serial Catalyst Center pagination or remove API rate limits. The preferred 500-record Device Health path cuts the five-cluster average from roughly 520–580 requests to 22–24 requests across both walks, and the Assurance Issue path removes the old N+1 enrichment design. These are still post-fix pilot configurations—not production capacity guarantees. Intervals above 900 seconds are not a general Device Health remedy because that input requests only the prior 15 minutes. ##### API input polling intervals * **Editable SD-WAN intervals:** Administrators can change the polling interval when editing any of the five SD-WAN API inputs. Site/Tunnel Details now uses the same editable numeric interval control as the other SD-WAN inputs. * **Existing guardrails preserved:** A positive integer is still required. Saving a value below the recommended interval displays the existing **Interval below recommended value** warning with **Cancel** and **Save anyway** choices. * **Cyber Vision parity verified:** All seven Cyber Vision API input forms include an editable interval, send it in the edit payload, and use REST handlers that accept the update. ##### SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring * **REST-only consolidated input:** **SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring** lets one stanza select several catalog dataset IDs and a device scope; authentication and collection stay on the SD-WAN Manager REST API with no device shell access. * **Stable event contract:** Every record uses `cisco:sdwan:realtime` and carries `dataset_id`, `dataset_label`, `monitoring_category`, `record_kind`, `endpoint_path`, `target_device_id`, `hostname`, `device_model`, `site_name`, `system_ip`, `tags`, `vmanage_host`, `collection_time`, and `schema_version`. Splunk `host` uses the lowercased device hostname when available. Dataset-aware eventtypes and tags map BFD sessions, routing sessions, hardware alerts, and performance records to appropriate CIM categories without creating hundreds of sourcetypes. * **One-call inventory enrichment:** One bounded `/dataservice/device` read per poll supplies the Devices-table identity fields for every selected dataset and powers the device selector. Enrichment is an in-memory system-IP lookup, not an API call per event or device. * **Category-filtered dataset selection:** Choosing a Real-Time Monitoring category narrows the dataset menu to that category. Existing selections from other categories remain visible only while selected so changing filters cannot silently remove them. * **Readable Cisco category names:** The category picker uses the catalog's human-readable Cisco domain labels instead of reconstructing names from machine slugs, preserving terms such as `DOT1x`, `IPv4 FIB`, `PPPoE`, `QoS`, and `SD-WAN`. * **Splunk-safe vendor fields:** Real-Time response keys cannot shadow Splunk metadata or TA-owned knowledge fields. Cisco's row-level `index` is emitted as `vendor_index`, leading `@` is removed from keys such as `@rid` (emitted as `rid`), and any future collision is retained with a `vendor_` prefix. The calculated `app=cisco_sdwan` field remains available for CIM and knowledge-object classification. This advances the Real-Time event envelope to schema version 2. * **Complete managed-device inventory:** Real-Time Monitoring lists and can target the full reachable Manager inventory, including SD-WAN Manager, SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), and SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) controllers as well as WAN Edges. The generic API Endpoint Collection remains WAN Edge-only. * **Bulk first, bounded fan-out:** All-device collection uses documented bulk state APIs for BFD Sessions, BGP Neighbors, Control Connections, Control Local Properties, Control WAN Interfaces, and Hardware Alarms. Other selected datasets fan out with a shared ten-request-per-second pace, at most five workers, bounded pagination, bounded records, and three attempts for rate-limit or server failures. * **Workload qualification:** The runtime estimates initial requests before data collection and limits the plan to 80% of the interval's paced request capacity, with a hard cap of 10,000 initial targets. The six-dataset recommended selection plans 5,006 initial requests for 5,000 devices at 900 seconds: one inventory call, five bulk calls, and 5,000 BFD History calls. Larger selections must be split, narrowed, or given a longer interval. * **History and partial failures:** History datasets use a per-input, per-dataset/device checkpoint with a five-minute overlap window and bounded recent hashes, preserving late arrivals while suppressing repeat records. Successful devices are still indexed when other dataset/device requests fail; the poll heartbeat reports `recovering` with success/failure and request metrics. * **No duplicate endpoint path:** Every catalog entry classified as Real-Time Monitoring is hidden from the generic SD-WAN API Endpoint Collection picker and rejected by its modular input. Existing generic custom sourcetypes remain unchanged for compatibility, while this dedicated input intentionally uses one stable sourcetype. ##### SD-WAN collection guidance * **Consolidated real-time collection:** **SD-WAN Real-Time Monitoring** selects several datasets in one stanza, supports one, selected, or all reachable managed devices including controllers, and emits one stable sourcetype with dataset identity fields. * **Bulk-first large-fleet behavior:** Six recommended datasets fit the 900-second admission guardrail for a representative 5,000-device fleet because five use documented controller-wide bulk state calls and BFD History uses bounded per-device fan-out. * **Scale and failure guardrails:** Shared request pacing, five workers, bounded retries, pagination and record caps, and an 80%-of-interval workload budget prevent an unbounded **Select all** pattern. Partial target failures preserve successful records and set the heartbeat to `recovering`. * **Checkpointed BFD history:** A per-input, per-dataset/device checkpoint with a five-minute overlap suppresses repeated history while preserving bounded late arrivals. * **Duplicate prevention:** Real-Time Monitoring paths are removed from the generic endpoint picker and rejected by the generic modular input. Both collectors enforce exact backend catalog IDs/paths, and neither exposes arbitrary URLs, device actions, or shell execution. * **Audit-log scope clarified:** The Audit Logs guidance now distinguishes SD-WAN Manager administrative and configuration activity from general device shell-command or operating-system process telemetry that the Manager does not expose through the audit-log API. * **ZBFW HSL recommendation clarified:** The guide now explicitly recommends High Speed Logging through NetFlow for production ZBFW pass/drop/inspect coverage because firewall text syslog is rate-limited and may not preserve every matching record under sustained load. * **HSL and syslog coexistence documented:** The guide now explains that HSL does not disable ordinary IOS-XE or UTD syslog, but becomes the primary export path for configured ZBFW event classes. Equivalent `%FW-*` duplicates must not be assumed, HSL pass notifications can still follow a configured rate limit, and Unified Logging changes pass/drop behavior on IOS XE SD-WAN 17.16.1a and later.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
## SCIP v1.2.14 — Detection Restoration, Compliance Status Accuracy, and Correlation Dedup Cumulative release covering all changes since v1.2.10, the previous published release. It consolidates work validated as v1.2.11 through v1.2.13, none of which were published separately. The most significant item is a critical AI/agentic threat detection defect; the remainder are compliance-evidence correctness fixes, an indexing-efficiency correction, and documentation accuracy. No new capabilities in this release. **Critical — AI/agentic threat detection restored:** - AI/agentic threat detection rules could silently produce zero results, with no error anywhere to indicate a problem. This has been corrected so all 10 of the included detection rules function as intended. No other detection or reporting behavior in the app was affected by this fix. **Compliance evidence accuracy:** - PCI DSS 6.4.1 and 6.4.2 (public-facing web application protection): the Compliance Gap Assessment dashboard could independently compute and display "Pass" for these two controls while the authoritative nightly compliance assessment had determined "Gap" for the same environment at the same time — the two surfaces used different data scopes, time windows, and aggregations. The dashboard no longer computes its own answer for these controls; it now displays only what the nightly assessment recorded, and shows an explicit "awaiting nightly compliance assessment" state when no assessment has run yet. The two surfaces can no longer disagree. - The count of AI/agentic threat detections feeding the PCI DSS 6.4.1/6.4.2 evidence checks and the dashboard summary was including only 10 of the app's 66 detection rules, understating actual detection coverage in compliance evidence. All 66 are now counted. - NIST SA-11: the federal compliance exports and the IL deployment guide each used a different non-official wording for this control's title. Both now use the official NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 title, "Developer Testing and Evaluation." SA-10 (Developer Configuration Management) and SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) descriptions were corrected in the README in the same pass. **Indexing efficiency:** - The NVD Version Range Correlation search was re-collecting every current version-range vulnerability match on each 2-hour run rather than writing each unique match once, unlike the two sibling correlation searches which already deduplicate. It now participates in the same deduplication ledger, so repeat runs no longer add duplicate entries to the alerts index or to downstream POA&M population. Genuinely new matches continue to be collected immediately. Existing installs will see index growth from this search level off; no customer action is required. **Dashboard consistency:** - Three dashboards (Supply Chain Risk Score, Compliance Gap Assessment, and SBOM Component Inventory) displayed their headline summary metrics inconsistently compared to the equivalent panels elsewhere in the app. All three now behave consistently with the rest of the product. **Documentation accuracy:** - The bundled OSV vulnerability lookup's ecosystem coverage was understated as 5 ecosystems; the bundled data actually covers 11 — PyPI, npm, Maven, Go, NuGet, crates.io, Packagist, RubyGems, SwiftURL, Pub, and Hex. The README and the About page now state the accurate count. - The About and Setup pages no longer imply that all 66 AI/agentic threat detection rules carry a MITRE ATLAS technique ID. The SPL Library provides a modern interface for storing, searching, and managing Splunk queries within the Splunk environment. The application features a dark card-based user interface that displays saved queries in an organized, searchable format. Users can perform full-text searches across query titles, descriptions, tags, and SPL content, and apply category filters to narrow results by Security, Network, Application, Database, Performance, or Other classifications. Each query card can be expanded to view the complete SPL code, copied to the clipboard with one click, or executed directly in the Splunk Search app. The application stores all queries in the Splunk KV Store, ensuring compatibility with Splunk Cloud deployments. Query management capabilities include adding, editing, and deleting entries through a modal form interface with tag assignment functionality. The application automatically seeds four example queries on initial deployment and records metadata including author information and creation/modification timestamps for each stored query. The architecture avoids custom REST handlers, external dependencies, and inline JavaScript, relying exclusively on Splunk-provided libraries and standard KV Store mechanisms for data persistence.

Release Notes:
Form Viz 2.3.9 is a backward-compatible update for Splunk Classic Dashboards. \- Adds checkbox multi-select, number, date, standalone Markdown, per-question Markdown descriptions, formatted read-only SPL display, and editable multiline SPL input. \- Saves complete, self-describing submissions, including blank answers, question order, field type, options, description, and a shared batch ID. \- Adds saved-response loading with Read Only and Edit in Place modes, including local and cross-app KV Store sources, latest-batch loading, and dashboard-token batch selection. \- Updates existing KV Store records safely by key while preserving submission identity and metadata owned by other workflows. Edits are blocked when required keys are missing. \- Adds configurable source and output app/lookup settings, display-order ranges, and per-panel mode tokens for dashboards containing multiple forms. \- Loads legacy responses that do not contain batch IDs or saved field metadata and retains the established form\_viz/form\_responses defaults. \- Handles duplicate question labels and missing order values independently, refreshes dependent searches only after confirmed writes, and displays actionable configuration and load errors. \- Improves token handling, direct-load limits, stale-request protection, resize stability, upgrade rollback, automated compatibility testing, and release validation. \- Replaces the crowded app navigation with an explanatory home dashboard and two focused Create and Review/Edit examples. Compatibility: Splunk Enterprise Classic Dashboards. Dashboard Studio is not supported in this V2 release.


Short Description:
Form Viz adds an interactive form visualization for Splunk Classic Dashboards, turning SPL results into form inputs and saving structured responses to KV Store for reporting, review, and workflow use.


Description:
Form Viz is a custom Splunk visualization for building interactive forms directly from SPL results or lookup-driven configuration. It solves the problem of collecting structured analyst input inside Splunk dashboards without building custom web pages or external apps. Form Viz can render text fields, dropdowns, radio buttons, checkboxes, dates, numbers, markdown guidance, and SPL review fields from simple rows containing question, type, options, order, and description values. Submitted responses are written to a Splunk KV Store collection with user, form name, question order, question text, answer, timestamp, and submission ID fields. This makes it useful for review workflows, triage forms, detection validation, saved search reviews, analyst notes, and other dashboard-based data collection tasks. The app includes example dashboards showing how to configure forms, use SPL display/input fields, and run a multi-section Saved Search Review workflow.
